n: Days after D&C 39, James Covel turned away. The Lord explains to Joseph and Sidney that Covel’s heart had been right when he covenanted to obey.

f.w: the heart of my servant James Covel was right before me

n: He received the word gladly, but Satan quickly tempted him, and fear of persecution and worldly cares led him to reject it — just like the seed on stony and thorny ground in Jesus’ parable.

f.w: received the word with gladness, but straightway

n: He broke his covenant, and his fate is in the Lord’s hands. A sobering reminder that good beginnings must be followed by endurance.
